- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is flat or trending down, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in bearish reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70) and forecast is still rising, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent low.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ negative sentiment days in row), model often underreacts — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for lagged bearish sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently below 70 and true outcome is above 75, increase forecast by 2–4% to reflect sentiment-driven rebound potential.
